name: Saints Marcellinus and Peter
history: A priest and an exorcist of Rome, martyred in the persecution of Diocletian and named every day in the Roman Canon. Pope Damasus wrote that as a boy he had heard the story of their deaths from the very man who beheaded them. Constantine built a basilica over their tomb, and his mother Helena was buried beside them.
life: Little is certain about Marcellinus and Peter beyond their deaths, but that little is unusually well attested. In the great persecution that began under Diocletian in 303, Marcellinus, a priest, and Peter, an exorcist, were arrested in Rome. Tradition holds that in prison they converted their jailer and his family. They were led to a wood outside the city, made to clear the ground where they would be buried, and beheaded there in secret, so that Christians would not find the place. The faithful found it all the same. Pope Damasus, later in the century, set up a verse inscription at their tomb, saying he had learned of their deaths from their executioner, who had himself become a Christian. Their catacomb on the Via Labicana, with its paintings, can still be visited, and the ruins of Helena’s mausoleum stand beside it.
prayerTo: Saints Marcellinus and Peter, you were killed in secret and your tomb was hidden, yet the Church remembers your names at every Mass. Pray for all who suffer unseen for Christ, for prisoners and those who guard them, and for me, that I may be faithful when no one is watching. Amen.
penance: Pray the Roman Canon slowly, or follow it attentively at Mass, and offer a prayer for those in prison and for prison officers.
meditation: Their killers chose a hidden place so they would be forgotten, and the hidden place became a shrine. What hidden faithfulness is God asking of you?
